key_symptoms: Runny nose; sneezing; mild cough; low-grade fever
red_flags: Fast or noisy breathing; fever above 39C lasting over 3 days; poor feeding
first_line_guidance: Supportive care: fluids and rest; see a pediatrician if red flags appear
notes: Source: WHO IMCI chart booklet (record edition)

key_symptoms: Ear pain; tugging at ear; fever; fussiness
red_flags: Ear discharge; severe pain; symptoms beyond 2-3 days
first_line_guidance: A pediatrician evaluates whether observation or antibiotics fit; do not start antibiotics on your own

key_symptoms: Wheeze; cough at night; shortness of breath with activity
red_flags: Blue lips; cannot speak full sentences; reliever needed very often
first_line_guidance: A pediatrician confirms diagnosis with lung-function tests and writes an action plan; families follow the written plan

red_flags: No urine for 6+ hours; sunken eyes; very sleepy; blood in stool
first_line_guidance: Oral rehydration solution (ORS) for fluid loss; seek care urgently if dehydration signs appear
notes: Source: WHO IMCI chart booklet (record edition)

red_flags: ANY fever in a neonate is a red flag by itself
first_line_guidance: Seek immediate medical care; do not wait or try home treatment first

red_flags: Blisters near eyes; breathing difficulty; infected-looking sores
first_line_guidance: Keep child home and comfortable; a pediatrician advises on itch relief and when to return; vaccine prevents most cases

key_symptoms: Barky cough; hoarse voice; worse at night
red_flags: Stridor at rest; drooling; blue lips; severe distress
first_line_guidance: Calm the child and use cool night air per pediatric guidance; urgent care if any red flag appears

key_symptoms: Runny nose then wheeze and cough; poor feeding
red_flags: Fast breathing; ribs showing with breaths; pauses in breathing
first_line_guidance: Supportive care with fluids and monitoring; hospitalization if breathing is labored; antibiotics do not treat viruses

key_symptoms: Infrequent hard stools; pain on passing stool; withholding
red_flags: Blood in stool; vomiting; swollen belly; weight loss
first_line_guidance: More fluids fiber and activity first; a pediatrician guides any laxative use; never dose laxatives yourself

key_symptoms: Dry itchy patches; worse in winter; family allergy history
red_flags: Oozing or crusted sores; spreading redness with fever; severe sleep loss
first_line_guidance: Regular moisturizers and trigger avoidance; a pediatrician grades severity and prescribes treatment
